text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.71% today to close at $427.34, continuing a sharp two-week decline of 10%. The stock was weighed down by today's announcement of quarterly earnings and a leadership change, landing as the broader refining sector faces mixed signals: US crude is trading at $103/barrel while global crude sits at $123/barrel, refineries are running at a healthy 92.8% capacity, but gasoline and diesel stockpiles remain relatively elevated. The earnings announcement coincided with analyst caution about Big Oil guidance — the actual forward outlook matters more than just reported profits in this cycle.

The two-week selloff also reflects uncertainty about the midterm election outcome and what a Democratic Congress could mean for energy policy, particularly the potential shift toward renewable energy investments that could reduce long-term demand for refined petroleum products.
